clue.text: Hobo managed fun runs in a piece of Somerset?

indicators.note: runs as in colours that run and blur, so the letters of the first three words bleed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tramp organises some fun on a stretch of West Country land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somerset' looks like the English county but is the novelist Somerset Maugham; a 'piece' of his is one of his books.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1915 novel by W. Somerset Maugham is a literary work, so a piece written by that Somerset.

clue.text: How to get food from a waiter out to lunch?

definitions.text: How to get food from a waiter
definitions.meaning: a waiter serves dessert taken from a wheeled cart

explanation.surface: A diner wonders how to get served by a waiter who has gone off for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mad, while literally food can be taken off a restaurant's serving cart.

clue.text: Try, after tax rises, to cheer

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: net pay is what remains after tax

explanation.surface: Someone attempts, after a tax increase, to raise spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like an order signal, but 'after tax' as a whole is the synonym, net pay being what is left once tax is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone up is to encourage them and lift their spirits.

clue.text: Papers theatrically exaggerate revolutionary Muslim leader

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: ID is identity papers
to ham is to overact

explanation.surface: The press sensationalises an insurgent Islamic figure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic belief this is the awaited redeemer; the title was also taken by the Sudanese rebel leader.

clue.text: Stood up cold topless Dutch egotist

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the word backwards

parts.note: to stand for election is to run, so stood is ran
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter

parts.note: my old Dutch is Cockney slang for one's wife, the missus

explanation.surface: A self-obsessed, chilly, half-naked Dutchman was left standing at the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAN into NAR; 'topless' cuts M from MISSUS to leave ISSUS. 'Dutch' is old London slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the youth fell in love with his own reflection, so his name means a self-admirer.

clue.text: See 1
Painter's reason to take the bus back?

indicators.note: back means the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: having no cab is a good reason to ride the bus

explanation.surface: An artist explains why he catches the bus home.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an Irish-born British artist known for his raw figurative canvases.

clue.text: One tending to brood and attack animal

parts.note: a nanny looks after a brood of children
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A minder of children turns on a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A female goat is a farm creature, a specific kind of beast.

clue.text: A European gets stuffed by British athlete

indicators.note: gets stuffed by means has something packed inside

parts.note: a Croat is a European from Croatia

explanation.surface: A continental sports star is beaten by a British rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets stuffed by' puts B inside A CROAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast or circus tumbler is an agile performer, a kind of sportsperson.

clue.text: Way of saving face, so only come in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise has its look changed, so these letters take a new form

explanation.surface: To avoid embarrassment, attend only if your identity is hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving face' looks like a single phrase, but 'face' is fodder and 'saving' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing in bulk lowers the unit cost, a business method of cutting expense.

clue.text: Large lady's eating last of cake, a little down

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside

parts.note: large means fat

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the word cake

parts.note: her is the possessive pronoun for a lady, as in the lady's or her

explanation.surface: A big woman tucks into the end of a cake, feeling slightly low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts E inside FAT. 'a little down' looks like mild sadness but is a single tuft of plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the soft plumage of birds, and one small piece of it is a single plume.

clue.text: Crook runs through life energetically

parts.note: a crook is a swindler, a con man or con

indicators.note: through means passing inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: bio is short for biography, a life story
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A criminal races through life with plenty of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' is the container signal: the runs abbreviation passes through the word for a life story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction means with vigour, a tempo marking telling players to perform with spirit.

clue.text: Navy tour in it at sea? Goodness!

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor exclaims in surprise at a naval voyage on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness!' reads as an exclamation, but it is the nourishing quality of food.
explanation.definitionFit: The goodness in food is its nourishing value, what the body takes from what is eaten.

clue.text: Flipping East End pastime includes nothing rough

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
flipping means turning over, so the pastime is read backwards

parts.note: a hobby, said with the dropped h of Cockney London's East End
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Cockney grumbles that a blasted local hobby involves no rough stuff at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a Cockney curse but reverses OBBY to YBBO, which 'includes' O. The East End of London is known for dropping the h.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, as a noun, is a lout or hooligan, the same as a British thug.

clue.text: Channel as start for sail across the Atlantic

indicators.note: start for takes the opening letter of sail

parts.note: seen from Britain, across the Atlantic is in America: in US

explanation.surface: A sailor names a waterway as the place to begin a transatlantic voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy this is a cavity or passage in bone or tissue, a channel through the body.

clue.text: Chap sadly back around houses in Spanish city

indicators.note: houses means holds inside
back means read in reverse

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow, said sadly
CA is circa, around
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man walks unhappily back through the houses of a city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALAS into SALA; SALA plus CA 'houses' MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This university city in western Spain is in Castile and León.

clue.text: Said what VIP spotter will do is fine in the main

indicators.note: said signals that the phrase is spoken and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: someone spotting a VIP will see a worthy, a notable person

explanation.surface: A celebrity spotter's habit is declared to be perfectly fine on the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea, the main being the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel fit for the open ocean is in good condition on the high seas, the main.

clue.text: Bad debts covered by firm; investor finally cheers up

indicators.note: in a down clue, covered by means placed underneath
in a down clue, up means reading upwards

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of investor

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, cheers
IOUs are written promises of debt

explanation.surface: A company takes on bad debts, yet the investor ends up cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses CO + R + TA to give ATROC; in a down clue 'covered by' puts IOUS underneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appalling or dreadful is very poor in quality.

clue.text: Aristotle tinkered with system for the better

indicators.note: something tinkered with is fiddled about, so the philosopher's name is reordered

explanation.surface: The Greek philosopher's ideas are adjusted to make a system that improves things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the better' looks like 'improvement' but is a person who bets, a bettor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tote, or pari-mutuel machine, is the betting system that pools gamblers' stakes and computes payouts.

clue.text: See 1
Instrument or article with two round objects

parts.note: the is the definite article
an orb and an O are both round objects

explanation.surface: A clue asks whether something is a tool or an item carrying two balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bass lute with extra strings, played in Baroque music.

clue.text: Bill ducks a subject to be ducked

parts.note: a bill in a bar or restaurant is a tab
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are two Os

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill avoids a topic everyone should avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batter's score of zero, so 'ducks' gives OO.
explanation.definitionFit: A forbidden topic is one people avoid raising, a matter to dodge in polite talk.

clue.text: Make a career in China, India or another country

indicators.note: in tells us the word for running sits inside the slang word for a mate

parts.note: china, from china plate, is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a bud
to career is to rush along, run
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a job in China, India or elsewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' means mate in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate). 'Make a career' looks like job-seeking but means run.
explanation.definitionFit: This landlocked African republic is a nation like China and India.

clue.text: See 8
Voiced disgust in music hall

indicators.note: voiced means spoken, so the word for disgust is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: odium is hatred or disgust

explanation.surface: Someone expresses revulsion at a music hall show.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome this was a roofed building for musical performances, a concert hall.

clue.text: Mastiff's tail wags around great group in pack

indicators.note: around means placed either side of something
the tail of the dog's name is its final letter

parts.note: wags are jokers, and so are cards, comical people
ace means excellent, great

explanation.surface: A big dog's tail swishes around while it runs with the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wags' looks like the tail's movement but means jokers; 'pack' is a deck of cards, not a group of dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings, queens and jacks are the court set within a deck of playing cards.

clue.text: Second home providing returns in the end

indicators.note: returns means the pieces read in reverse

parts.note: at home is in
providing means if

explanation.surface: A holiday home ultimately pays off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word printed at the close of a book or film marks the finish.

clue.text: Pull in outside of Lille, stopping vehicle

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so going inside

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: outside of takes the outer letters of Lille

explanation.surface: A driver halts their car on the edge of Lille.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull in' looks like stopping a vehicle but means earning money; 'stopping' is the container signal, plugging the vehicle with the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To take home money after deductions is to net or earn it.

clue.text: It helps to see nurse with eccentric clothing

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around something

parts.note: a loon is a crazy or eccentric person
RGN stands for Registered General Nurse

explanation.surface: A carer in odd attire offers to help with eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' is the container signal. The nurse is a British Registered General Nurse, abbreviated to its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of spectacles held by a handle is an aid to vision, an opera glass of sorts.

clue.text: To the west, a cool and a green Pacific region

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
eco means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: Heading west, a fresh green landscape appears in a Pacific territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers Australia, New Zealand and the island groups of the central and southern Pacific.

clue.text: Great aid agreed, keeping Arab land waiting

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: agreed is the reply yes
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula
waiting at table is service

explanation.surface: Big aid was approved, though an Arab country is left waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' is the container signal: the affirmative reply holds the Gulf sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sterling, valuable assistance, after the reliable service of yeomen.

clue.text: See 27
